name: Chiplets and advanced semiconductor packaging
summary: Multiple specialized dies are assembled into one package so a computing system can grow beyond the practical limits of a single large chip.
useCase: An AI processor combines compute chiplets, high-bandwidth memory and networking interfaces in an advanced package.
whyNow: AI systems need more memory bandwidth and larger effective silicon areas. Packaging, interconnect design and thermal management therefore have strategic value alongside transistor scaling. The UCIe standard progressed from its initial 2022 specification to version 3.0 in 2025, doubling maximum link speed to 64 GT/s. A standard’s capability is evidence of technical progress, not proof that an open chiplet marketplace already exists.

mainstream.scope: Advanced multi-die packaging as a routine design choice for high-performance AI, server and selected automotive chips.
mainstream.rationale: Commercial multi-die products and a maturing interface standard support the window. This scope includes tightly controlled vendor ecosystems. Freely mixing third-party chiplets has harder validation, yield, warranty and business-model problems and may take longer than mainstream advanced packaging itself.

direction: Accelerating; packaging becomes a capacity constraint

metric.name: Maximum UCIe link rate — technical capability proxy
metric.scope: Maximum per-lane transfer rate supported by published UCIe specifications.
metric.limitations: Standards capability, not shipped products, adoption, realized bandwidth or package revenue. A higher supported rate is only useful if manufacturers achieve yield, signal integrity and acceptable power. Missing 2021 and 2026 adoption counts are not inferred.
metric.futureNote: There is no adopted future UCIe data rate in this dataset. Future progress should be assessed through qualified products, packaging capacity, yield and interoperability demonstrations.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No UCIe specification existed in the series; earlier proprietary multi-die designs are outside this KPI.
UCIe’s initial specification established a common die-to-die interface framework.
The consortium exceeded 100 members and released UCIe 1.1.
UCIe 2.0 added provisions for 3D packaging and system manageability.
UCIe 3.0 raised supported transfer rates to 48 and 64 GT/s.
The consortium continued implementation and foundry updates; Eliyan announced a new private financing round.

tailwinds: Different functions can use the fabrication process best suited to their cost and performance.
High-bandwidth memory and large AI designs raise the value of advanced assembly and testing.
bottlenecks: Packaging yield, heat extraction, substrates and testing are difficult at larger system scale.
Interoperability requires electrical, logical, security and commercial agreement across suppliers.
watchMetrics: Qualified advanced-package capacity, lead times and package-level yield.
Number of interoperable multi-vendor products shipped, separate from consortium membership and test chips.
